items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: Early 80’s I guess, was Phil Woods and Lew Tabackin. And the rhythm section was me and Michael Moore on bass and Jimmy Rowles on piano.

ctx.x: Have you been in a situation as a producer, this might be more of a pop thing where you had to really hype somebody up to get in there, “You can do it, you can do it.”?

Well occasionally, mostly some really old guy who is out of his gourd I think without defaming him I think there was a session I did pretty early on in the ‘70s in my producing career or early ‘80s. Early 80’s I guess, was Phil Woods and Lew Tabackin. And the rhythm section was me and Michael Moore on bass and Jimmy Rowles on piano. And Jimmy had taken the — had left home in L.A. and moved in to New York and was living with Carol Sloane the singer and had gone on the road — had taken the gig with Ella Fitzgerald.…

I’ve often wondered about that. Sometimes you see a record where it’s a quartet except for one song that’s a trio. Like no chordal instrument. And you think, “Oh that was very experimental for them” when in fact probably the piano player just couldn’t finish.
